Agriculture, forestry & nature

Estate boundaries, forest cover and fire, mapped from the air

Dated records of what has changed across your estate, plantation, offset or reserve, and at its boundary: cleared ground, new tracks and structures, burnt areas and revegetation, drawn from satellite data and reviewed by a person before they reach you.

Send us your estate, plot or offset boundaries Imagery and data sources

The problem, in your words

Large areas, few people, and change at the edges

Estates, plantations, conservation areas and offsets cover far more ground than any team can patrol. Clearing, new tracks and structures appear at the boundary, fire moves through in the dry season, and buyers, certifiers, lenders and funders increasingly ask for dated evidence of what the land looked like, and when.

“Clearing and new tracks keep appearing at the boundary.”

Estate and reserve managers need to know where and roughly when the edge changed, before it becomes a dispute.

“Our buyers want plot histories.”

Exporters and their EU customers need dated evidence of what each plot looked like against the deforestation-free cut-off date.

“We have to show the offset is working.”

Offset and restoration programmes need a dated trend of land cover and disturbance that their reviewers and funders can check.

Who this is for

  • Plantation and estate managers, and fire managers
  • Certification and sustainability managers
  • Exporters’ and EU importers’ due-diligence teams
  • REDD+ and restoration developers’ MRV and GIS leads
  • Biodiversity-offset and protected-area managers
  • Programme M&E teams

Estates and plantations

Boundaries, clearing and fire across the estate

We map structures inside your estate boundary and in a ring around it, and flag new structures, cleared ground and new tracks at the boundary between dated surveys, with fence lines and gates checked by a reviewer on drone imagery where flown. Vegetation and land-cover change across the estate is compared between dates from Copernicus Sentinel data, and regular forest-loss and ground-disturbance alerts from global systems are checked by our team and sent as notices.

In the fire season, satellite-detected fire hotspots near your blocks are filtered to your boundaries, checked and sent as notices, followed by maps of the burnt area. Revegetation on replanted or restored blocks is followed between dates, and a land-cover baseline and the estate’s imagery history show what the land looked like before.

What you receive

  • Structures inside the estate and in a ring around it
  • Boundary change: new structures, clearing and tracks
  • Vegetation and land-cover change between dates
  • Checked forest-loss and disturbance notices
  • Fire-hotspot notices and burnt-area maps
  • A land-cover baseline and imagery history

Deforestation-free supply chains

Plot histories against the EUDR cut-off date

The EU Deforestation Regulation asks operators placing cocoa, rubber, palm oil and other listed commodities on the EU market to show that the land was not deforested after 31 December 2020 (European Commission). For each plot you supply, we assemble a dated history from archived satellite imagery and open datasets, check tree-cover loss and disturbance alerts against the cut-off date, and add a land-cover baseline and the structures inside and around the plot.

The results come as a GIS layer per plot, with the evidence for each, ready for your own due-diligence system. We can also analyse imagery you already hold for your plots.

What a plot history is, and is not

A dated record of what the imagery and open data show for a plot. It is not a due-diligence statement, it does not make a plot compliant, and the plot boundaries are supplied or checked by you.

Imagery history & land due diligence

What was on a parcel, route or site, and roughly when, from archived satellite imagery and open datasets.

Carbon and landscape restoration

Dated land-cover records for restoration programmes

REDD+ and restoration programmes need a baseline and a dated trend. We deliver a land-cover baseline, forest-loss and disturbance alerts, vegetation change and revegetation between dates, radar comparisons that show larger changes even under rainy-season cloud, settlement growth trends around the project area and the area’s imagery history. Where benefit-sharing plans need them, a dated register of structures and estimated households supports that planning, with the assumptions stated.

These records support your monitoring, reporting and verification. We give no carbon tonnage and no verification opinion.

Settlement & household estimates

Structure layers and estimated households for mini-grid sizing, service planning and consultation planning, with the assumptions stated.

Offsets and protected areas

Disturbance, tracks and structures inside reserves and offsets

Biodiversity offsets and protected areas are often remote, and some are insecure, which makes satellite-first records the practical route. We map land-cover change, disturbance alerts, revegetation, fire and burnt areas, and flag new structures, cleared ground and tracks at the boundary and inside it. Radar comparisons show larger changes even under rainy-season cloud. Surface excavations inside a reserve, such as pits and spoil, are mapped between dates.

It shows larger patches of change, not individual trees or species, and it is not an ecological survey.

Land, never people or animals

We map land cover, clearing, tracks, structures and excavations. We do not detect people or livestock, and anti-poaching, guarding and security response are outside what we do.

Excavation & ground-disturbance mapping

Pits, fresh digging, spoil heaps and new tracks mapped between dates, so your field teams know where to check.

Mozambique, South Africa, Nigeria

Where the rules shape the record

A summary for orientation, as of 26 September 2026, not legal advice; the sources are linked.

Português · English

Mozambique

Biodiversity offsets for Category A and A+ projects are required under the offsets directive (Diploma Ministerial n.º 55/2022), with BIOFUND implementing the national biodiversity offsets programme. Many reserves are remote and some are insecure, so satellite-first records let monitoring start without a site visit. Reports can be delivered in Portuguese.

English

South Africa

Estates already have strong fire systems through fire protection associations and the CSIR’s AFIS, so our work there leads with boundary, clearing and land-cover change rather than fire. Over special nature reserves and world heritage sites, the Protected Areas Act (s47) restricts flights below 2,500 ft, so work there is planned as satellite-only.

English

Nigeria

The EU Deforestation Regulation matters most for Nigerian cocoa, rubber and palm oil, where exporters and their EU buyers need plot histories against the cut-off date. Remote, satellite-first records suit plots spread across many smallholdings and states.

Honest scope

What we do, and what we don’t

What we do

  • Map clearing, regrowth, burnt areas, tracks and structures, compared between dates
  • Filter fire hotspots and disturbance alerts to your boundaries, and check them
  • Assemble dated plot histories against a cut-off date
  • Supply records that support certification, MRV and offset reporting

What we don’t do

  • Survey species, count trees or assess ecological condition
  • Look for people or livestock, or run anti-poaching or security services
  • Issue due-diligence statements, verification opinions or carbon figures
  • Provide an emergency or early-warning fire service

Frequently asked questions

Can you see individual trees or species?

No. Satellite land-cover work shows larger patches of change, such as clearing, regrowth and burnt areas, not individual trees or species. It is not an ecological or species survey. Drone surveys show more detail where flown.

Can you make our supply chain EUDR-compliant?

No. We supply dated plot histories against the Regulation’s cut-off date, from archived imagery and open data, for your own due diligence. The due-diligence statement, and the plot boundaries themselves, stay with you.

Do you verify carbon or offset outcomes?

No. We supply dated land-cover and change records that support your monitoring, reporting and verification. We give no carbon tonnage and no verification opinion, and we never state that an offset has achieved no net loss.

Do you track poachers, people or livestock?

No. We map land and assets only. Anti-poaching, guarding and security response are outside what we do.

How current are the alerts?

Alerts come from global satellite alert systems, such as Global Forest Watch, on the cycle those systems publish. We check them and send a regular notice for your area. They are indications to check on the ground or on higher-resolution imagery, not proof, and they will not catch every disturbance.

Send us your estate, plot or offset boundaries

Boundaries as KML, GeoJSON or Shapefile, and what the record is for, are enough to scope a baseline and scheduled change notices.
